unit_description: This unit introduces scaled picture graphs and bar graphs. Students read and create scaled graphs and solve one- and two-step problems using data from graphs.
unit_goals: Create scaled graphs and solve one- and two-step problems.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students learn to read and create scaled picture and bar graphs and use them to solve problems.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting symbols and using a key.
lessons.concept: A picture graph uses symbols to show data. When the graph is scaled, each symbol stands for more than one. Use the key to find the value of the symbols.
lessons.practice: Read scaled picture graphs and answer questions.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with a picture graph.

questions.prompt: A picture graph key says each star = 5 books. If a student has 3 stars, how many books?
A picture graph key says each apple = 2 students. How many students for 4 apples?
If each symbol = 4 and there is half a symbol, what does it stand for?

learn.title: Read Scaled Picture Graphs
teaching_points: Read the key to see what each symbol stands for.
Count the symbols for each category.

example.prompt: A picture graph shows books read. Each book symbol = 3. Alex has 4 symbols. How many books?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A picture graph key says each star = 4 points. A team has 5 stars. How many points?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Use the key to answer questions about each picture graph.

bigIdea.title: Read Scaled Picture Graphs
bigIdea.subtitle: Use the key
bigIdea.intro: In a scaled picture graph, each picture stands for more than one. Always look at the key to know how many each symbol represents.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why do scaled picture graphs use keys?

ruleCards.description: The key tells you how many items each symbol represents.
Count the symbols and multiply by the key value.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by choosing a good scale for a data set.
lessons.concept: To create a scaled picture graph, choose a key, such as 1 symbol = 2 or 5, and draw the correct number of symbols for each category.
lessons.practice: Create scaled picture graphs from data tables.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by creating a picture graph.

questions.prompt: If 15 students like apples and the key is 1 apple = 5, how many apple symbols?
If 20 students like soccer and 1 ball = 4, how many ball symbols?
If 8 students like dogs and 1 dog symbol = 2, how many symbols?

learn.title: Create Scaled Picture Graphs
teaching_points: Pick a scale that makes the graph easy to read.
Divide each value by the scale to find the number of symbols.
Label the key and categories clearly.

example.prompt: Create a picture graph for favorite fruits: apples 12, bananas 8, grapes 16. Use 1 fruit = 4.
example.equation: apples 3 symbols, bananas 2 symbols, grapes 4 symbols

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Create a picture graph for pets: dogs 10, cats 15, fish 5. Use 1 paw = 5.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Choose a key and draw a scaled picture graph for each data set.

bigIdea.title: Create Scaled Picture Graphs
bigIdea.subtitle: Pick a good scale
bigIdea.intro: When you make a picture graph, choose a scale that keeps the number of symbols small and easy to count. Divide each number by the scale to find how many symbols to draw.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you choose a good scale for a picture graph?

ruleCards.description: Pick a scale that gives a small number of symbols.
Divide each value by the scale.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by reading heights of bars on a scaled bar graph.
lessons.concept: A bar graph uses bars to show data. On a scaled bar graph, the scale may count by 2, 5, or 10. Use the scale to read the value of each bar.
lessons.practice: Read scaled bar graphs and answer questions.

questions.prompt: A bar graph scale counts by 5. A bar reaches 4 spaces. How many?
A bar graph scale counts by 10. A bar reaches 6 spaces. How many?
Which is taller: a bar at 30 or a bar at 45?

learn.title: Read Scaled Bar Graphs
teaching_points: Look at the scale on the side.
Find how high each bar goes.
Multiply the height by the scale.

example.prompt: A bar graph shows number of books. Scale counts by 2. The bar for June reaches 7 spaces.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A bar graph scale counts by 5. The bar for dogs reaches 8 spaces. How many dogs?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Read each bar graph and answer the questions.

bigIdea.title: Read Scaled Bar Graphs
bigIdea.subtitle: Use the scale on the side
bigIdea.intro: On a scaled bar graph, each line may stand for more than one. Find the top of the bar, read across to the scale, and multiply to find the value.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is a scaled bar graph like a picture graph?

ruleCards.description: The scale tells how much each space represents.
Multiply the number of spaces by the scale.

lessons.lesson_title: Create Graphs and Solve One- and Two-Step Problems
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by solving addition and subtraction questions from a simple bar graph.
lessons.concept: Graphs help answer questions. One-step problems ask for a single value. Two-step problems may ask you to combine or compare values from the graph.
lessons.practice: Create scaled graphs from data and solve one- and two-step problems.
lessons.objective: Create scaled graphs and solve one- and two-step problems using data.

questions.prompt: A graph shows 10 red, 15 blue, and 5 green marbles. How many more blue than green?
A graph shows 12 cars, 8 trucks, and 10 bikes. How many vehicles total?
If twice as many students like soccer than baseball, and 6 like baseball, how many like soccer?

learn.title: Create Graphs and Solve One- and Two-Step Problems
teaching_points: Do one or two operations to answer the question.

example.prompt: Create a bar graph for votes: pizza 20, tacos 15, burgers 10. How many more voted for pizza than burgers?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A bar graph shows points: Team A 25, Team B 15, Team C 10. What is the total and how many more points does Team A have than Team C?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Create a graph from the data and solve the problems.

bigIdea.title: Create Graphs and Solve One- and Two-Step Problems
bigIdea.subtitle: Graphs help answer questions
bigIdea.intro: After making a graph, you can use it to answer questions. One-step questions use one value. Two-step questions may add, subtract, or compare values.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do graphs help solve two-step problems?

ruleCards.description: Read the value from the graph.

ruleCards.equation: How many more for pizza than burgers?

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of reading picture graphs, creating picture graphs, reading bar graphs, and solving graph problems.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: reading scaled picture graphs, creating scaled picture graphs, reading scaled bar graphs, and creating graphs to solve one- and two-step problems.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about scaled picture and bar graphs.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: A picture graph key says each star = 5. If a student has 3 stars, how many?
A bar graph scale counts by 10. A bar reaches 5 spaces. What is the value?
A graph shows 12 cats, 8 dogs, and 10 birds. How many more cats than dogs?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: read picture graphs + create picture graphs + read bar graphs + solve problems = scaled graphs

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A bar graph scale counts by 5. A bar reaches 6 spaces. What is the value?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 25 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 25 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Scaled Graphs
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: reading scaled picture graphs, creating scaled picture graphs, reading scaled bar graphs, and solving one- and two-step problems with graphs.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about scaled graphs?

ruleCards.equation: key tells value of each symbol
ruleCards.description: Multiply the number of symbols by the key value.

ruleCards.equation: scale tells value of each space
ruleCards.description: Multiply the bar height by the scale value.
